title: SPECTRUM COEXISTENCE LABORATORY (ARTES 4.0 SPL 4S 3A.229) - EXPRO+
description: The objective is to develop a standardised test laboratory to evaluate the coexistence of various satellite and terrestrial systemswithin a realistic, emulated, and controlled environment.TargetedImprovements: Enable a quantified and objective assessment of mutual interferences. Reduce satcom service outage due to interference from third systems to less than 0.1%.Description: Traditional methods of interference analysis and simulation, which often rely on static models and assumptions, are insufficient to describe thereal-time interactions and variability ofsatellite and terrestrial telecommunication networks. For example, in assessing the potential interference of new NGSO systems, it is mandatory to describe the dynamic radio resourceallocation strategy of the NGSO systemunder test to assess its dynamic effects on incumbent systems such as NGSO, GSO, or terrestrial mobile networks. Moreover, current analysistools are limited to assessing the interaction between the system under test and specific victim incumbent systems, ignoring the rest of the environment, i.e. additional incumbent systemsthat may also be affected. A standardised coexistence test laboratory is essential to address these challenges. By providing a controlled environment that accurately emulates real-worldoperational scenarios, this laboratory will enable a comprehensive evaluation of spectrum coexistence. The use of standardised plug-in modules, interfaces (e.g. API, RF, IF, DIFI), anddescriptors will facilitate the modelling of various satellite and terrestrial systems and their interactions, ensuring that the assessments are both accurate and confidential. The integrationwith external RF monitoring datasets will enable a digital synthesis of the RF spectrum to establish a background digital (and protected, i.e. sandbox) environment where the tests canbe performed.This activity will develop a test laboratory comprising hardware and software components following amodular and hierarchical approach, enabling future extensibility as well as follow-up/parallel developments. The activity will first establish a development framework, including development guidelines and requirements as well as interface specifications, and thendevelop key modules sufficient to provide an initial service.

title: CAN BACKPLANE INTERFACE MEZZANINE BOARD - EXPRO PLUS
description: To build a mezzanine board to interface with a CAN bus on the units' backplane.Description:As part of the APA (Advanced Power Architecture) initiative, a standardised approach is being developed for internal communication between APA modules within an APA unit. This activity supports that effort by designing a compact, reusable TM/TC interface based on the CAN bus, known for itsreliabilityand simplicity.The mezzanine will serve as a common building block / solution for all APA modules, reducing integration effortandpromoting consistency across designs. By consolidating all required components into a small footprint, it simplifies system architecture, supports modularity and eases procurement, manufacturing and recurrence.This activity focuses on developing a compact mezzanine PCB that integrates five essential components required for CAN-based backplane communication (FPGA or microcontroller, ADC, voltage reference, CAN transceiver and XTAL/oscillator). The goal is to consolidate these elements into a small 30x30 mm footprint, supporting a range of external interfaces and operating on a 3.3V supply.This modular solution aims to simplify internal communication across systems where CAN is the preferred protocol, offering a reusable and scalable interface.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Consolidate the CAN protocol implementation.- Architecture definition (evaluating if FPGA-based or microcontroller-based).- Identify two suitable options for each one of the 5 required components, prioritising compact packaging and cost.- Design a 30mm x 30 mm PCB accommodating the 5 components and ensuring signal integrity andmanufacturability, ready to be assembled into an APA module and to interface with CAN bus and the APA module.- Implement the software or the VHDL code with the CAN protocol.- Prototyping and testing, assemble and validate the board to confirm functionality and performance.Deliverables: Breadboard,ReportNOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: RADIATION EFFECTS INSIDE THE SPACECRAFT COMPATIBLE WITH ADHA DEVELOPMENT- EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a breadboard of a radiation detection unit based on Advanced Data Handling Architectures (ADHA) in order to minimise on-board resources, while improving the integration and deployment.Description: The Agency has had success developing and flying radiation monitors, starting with the REM in the 90's, the SREM in the 2000s, and the EMU and NGRMs since 2017. These monitors have all been self contained and externally mounted, with masses and power requirements exceeding 1 kg and 2 W - low resource, butnot insignificant. Some of these instruments have housed dosimeters, but none have provided measurements within the other spacecraft units. At the moment, there are no low resource radiation monitors available capable of integration within the spacecraft and its units where the sensitive systems are located and capable to provide useful, unparalleled feedback to satellite operations. The benefits include enabled monitoring of the spacecraft health, and providing useful operational diagnostics, and accurate information on the environment. Radiation monitors are the first modules to be discarded during phase A of design due to additional mass and power budget constraints. This disrupts the huge potential of in-orbit data collection, which affects radiation model accuracy and uncertainty a measure, Radiation monitor will allow to manage approach to radiation effects, potentially extending mission lifetimes and opening the door to widespread use of COTS. It is envisaged that this should become standard on all platforms as part of S/C 'health' data - as is already done with thermal measurements. In order to enhance the European competitiveness for LEO applications for mid-size satellites, it is aimed to design and test a portfolio of standardized dosimeters and memories. By including the radiation monitors in the Advanced Data Handling architecture (ADHA), standardized, interchangeable, and inter-operable electronics modules equipped with the latest generation of microelectronics components can be integrated within the spacecraft units. Components and commercialprocesses from European foundries and manufacturers shall be baselined for dose measurements. Several configuration can be considered: detection unit embedded into each ADHA board, detection unit placed at different point of ADHA or to be considered as a standalone board. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - A trade-off shall be made between of the different solutions considered -Breadboarding and functional testing - Total ionising Dose and SEE testing - Roadmap to fully characterise and fly European memories once they become availableDeliverables: Breadboard, Report

title: LIGHT CONDUCTION AND DIFFUSION MATERIALS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF LIGHT INTENSIFIED PHOTOBIOREACTORS
description: ObjectivesTo increase the efficiency of photobioreactors by an improved design of light conduction anddiffusion inside the reactor.DescriptionThe need for regenerative life support systems for long term space missions necessitates a questfor increased efficiency of Photobioreactors. The light intensification of photobioreactors is animportant building block to increase the return on investment with respect to light energy introducedvs oxygen yield in a defined volume.Previous activities have identified as a priority the need to progress on specific technologies, suchas the type of light sources and on innovative materials for light conductionand diffusion (e.g.polymers, leaking rods, specific optical fibers, lightning fabrics). This activity attempts to push theboundaries of photobioractor efficiency even further (compared to BIORAT-1) by investigating amore efficient light diffusion and as well characterization of the impact on the process and thebiomass.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review the state of the art for light intensified photobioreactiors and energy efficient lightguidance systems- Design a test bench with realistic operational parameters (light, flow, active species etc.)and test the most optimal configuration to achieve best possible efficiency w.r.t. volumetricoxygen and biomass production- Assess the potential biological effects of immersed light sources and possiblecountermeasures against fouling and clogging- Provide a development plan for operational hardware on ground and in space includingMAIT aspects for an operational scenario and define the scaling laws.
